messages.subject: Multigroup Path Analysis Modification Indices
parts:
I am running a path analysis with 5 groups.  I built an overall model, with great fit indices, but the fit indices are terrible for the multigroup model. The overall model is uninteresting and not the point of the research. 

I went through the invariant testing steps to find that my model is best left with just the configuration model. 

In order to improve the model fit for each group, I was hoping to use the modificationIndices() to improve individual groups by adjusting the covariance structure within each group.  I can't figure out how to code this.

I attempted the below example with quotes in the model code itself, and NA replacing the 0 with no luck.  I was hoping this would free the covariance in the 5th group, and constrain the covariance to the first 4 groups to be equal, its not working. 

(similar to constraining the factor loadings here: https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html)

#covariance
x ~~ c(a,a,a,a,NA)*y

Within the sem() code I also tried the below, though this frees it up across all groups, not individual groups.
group.equal = c("residual.covariances"),
group.partial = ( x ~~ y) 
~~~~
Model:  I can't share my data, but I made a similar enough example out of the iris dataset. I copied my specific coding and changed the variables
mod<-'
   
     #Direct Effects
       sepal.length ~ c("a","a","a")*Petal.Length + Petal.Width
       sepal.wideth ~ c("e","e","e","e","e") *Petal.Length + Petal.Width
     
     #Fix the variance to 1
     Petal.Length       ~~ 1*Petal.Length
     Petal.Width        ~~ 1*Petal.Width

     #covariances
        Petal.Length ~~ c(a,a,NA)*Sepal.Width
        Sepal.Width ~~ Sepal.Length
  # '
    
 group.model.b <- sem(model = mod,
                         data = iris,
                         meanstructure = TRUE,#this is important
                         group="Species",
                         missing="fiml")

 After removing  c(a,a,NA)* from the model,   I also tried the belwo, but I know that is not exactly what I need, it alows the covariance to be freely estimated across all groups, not a particular group.
 group.model.c <- sem(model = mod,
                         data = iris,
                         meanstructure = TRUE,#this is important
                         group="Species",
                         missing="fiml",
                         group.equal = c("residual.covariances"),
                         group.partial= c("Petal.Length ~~ c(Sepal.Width")
